summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package ships an inert Proxy no-op as its main export and a postinstall script (beacon.cjs) that POSTs a JSON payload containing the installer's hostname, install path, current working directory, and Node version to the hardcoded plaintext HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The same beacon is also invoked from index.js, so it fires again whenever any consumer calls require('nitro-bundled-dep'). The destination is a bare IP over cleartext HTTP with no first-party domain, no TLS, and no opt-in. The package provides no functional library surface — its only effect on install and import is to transmit host identifiers to a hardcoded non-publisher endpoint. The name shape (looking like a bundled internal dependency) combined with the inert API and automatic callback is consistent with a dependency-confusion / unsolicited install-tracking payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
